title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
author: Anouar Imel, Imad Charradi, Abderrahman Sghir, Khalil El Khammar
description: When an LLM group's discussion is compressed into a short memory for a final decision maker, what should the memory keep? summary: When an LLM group's discussion is compressed into a short memory for a final decision maker, what should the memory keep? Two natural heuristics keep the rarest claims or the claims relevant to the decision criteria.
takeaways: The decision model adds a third failure, a form of social proof: it gives extra weight to facts attributed to many agents.
Two natural heuristics keep the rarest claims or the claims relevant to the decision criteria.

We introduce CrossProfile, a diagnostic benchmark of 60 templates with automatically verified answer keys, in which the ownership of supporting, decoy, and irrelevant facts is crossed while their text is held fixed (480 tasks).
